overview: This two-page internal list of papers indexes U.S. diplomatic and interdepartmental correspondence from 1934–1938 concerning the inspection of merchant vessels in Japan. Most entries record Japanese appointments and removals of ship inspectors authorized to issue Panama Canal tonnage certificates; the remainder concern Japanese ship-inspection laws, inspection fees imposed in Japanese ports, and a Commerce Department request for diplomatic action or reciprocal charges. The index identifies relevant despatches, notes, enclosures, instructions, and cross-references to related files.

subfiles.title: List of papers concerning inspection of merchant vessels in Japan
subfiles.about: An internal index describes correspondence from 1934–1938 about Japanese ship inspectors, Panama Canal tonnage certification, and the inspection of American and other foreign vessels in Japanese ports.
subfiles.summary: The first group of entries records the appointment or removal of Japanese inspectors empowered to issue or sign Panama Canal tonnage certificates. Other entries refer to reports on Japanese ship-inspection laws and fees, including missing or subsequently transmitted enclosures. The Commerce Department requested negotiations to exempt American vessels from Japanese inspection charges and threatened reciprocal fees if no agreement could be reached; later correspondence reported that American ships were not charged for inspections required of foreign vessels under Japanese law.

interest: The index is useful for reconstructing a dispersed administrative correspondence whose underlying papers may now be located elsewhere in the decimal file. It documents the personnel infrastructure through which Japanese authorities certified vessels under Panama Canal rules and also reveals how routine inspection charges could become an issue of diplomatic reciprocity. Its references to omitted enclosures, related file 195.4, and copies forwarded to the Panama Canal and Commerce Department provide valuable leads for tracing the complete documentary record.
